edges.description: Channel-deficient rods accumulate cGMP; gene augmentation reverses this in treated retina.
Loss of rod function precedes progressive rod death in CNGA1-deficient mice; the intermediates connecting channel loss to death are not fully resolved.
Loss of rod-mediated vision impairs vision in dim light.
Loss of the rod light response removes the rod-driven ERG; later cone loss extinguishes the remaining photopic response.
Abnormal cGMP accumulation is proposed to contribute to rod death; the causal step has not been isolated in CNGA1 models.
Cone function and structure decline after rod loss; the non-cell-autonomous intermediates are unresolved.
Progressive loss of peripheral photoreceptors narrows the visual field.
Pigment migrates into the degenerating retina and clumps in a bone-spicule pattern as photoreceptors are lost.
Retinal vessel attenuation is a secondary change of long-standing retinal degeneration.
Waxy disc pallor reflects long-standing retinal degeneration.
Rod-first, cone-second degeneration produces the rod-cone dystrophy pattern.
Loss of central cone function reduces visual acuity, usually after the third decade; cataract and macular complications also contribute.
Advanced disease extends to the macula with atrophic and pigmentary changes.
Loss of cones removes the residual photopic response, leaving a nonrecordable ERG in most adult patients.

nodes.description: Investigational. Subretinal AAV8-hRHO-mCnga1 restores rod function, reverses cGMP accumulation and preserves photoreceptors in the Cnga1 knockout mouse. An intravitreal AAV2.NN-CNGA1 vector (VG901) is in a phase 1b open-label safety study in patients. Human efficacy has not been established.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic CNGA1 variants remove or disable the alpha subunit of the rod cGMP-gated channel. Early nonsense and frameshift alleles and whole-gene deletion are expected to encode no functional channel; missense and distal frameshift alleles that have been expressed in vitro reduce membrane targeting, abundance or channel function. Not every reported missense variant is pathogenic, and functional testing has reclassified many variants of uncertain significance.

evidence.snippet: Two of these were nonsense mutations early in the reading frame (Glu76End and Lys139End) and one was a deletion encompassing most if not all of the transcriptional unit; these three alleles would not be expected to encode a functional channel.

evidence.snippet: The aequorin-based assay showed that 72.1% of tested variants significantly impaired CNG channel function and were classified as functionally abnormal, while 23.3% were functionally normal and 5% remained functionally uncertain.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic germline CNGA1 variants, homozygous or compound heterozygous; most are truncating, with a smaller set of missense alleles shown to impair channel expression or function.

nodes.description: The native rod channel is a 3:1 CNGA1:CNGB1 heterotetramer in the outer-segment plasma membrane. Mutant CNGA1 proteins expressed in vitro are retained inside the cell or reach the membrane at reduced levels, and one C-terminal frameshift abolishes surface expression only when coexpressed with CNGB1. In a Cnga1 point-mutant mouse, CNGA1 protein is lost and the CNGB1 partner protein is also undetectable despite normal transcript levels, so the outer segment lacks the channel complex.

nodes.description: Rods degenerate after loss of function. In the CRISPR Cnga1 knockout the outer nuclear layer thins almost linearly and is nearly gone by 6 months, with TUNEL-positive photoreceptors, microglial activation and oxidative damage, and transcriptomic evidence of reduced PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling with chaperone-mediated autophagy coinciding with photoreceptor death. The Y509C point mutant degenerates more slowly. In patients, ellipsoid-zone width declines over years and fundus changes of retinitis pigmentosa accumulate.
